methodology: Articles sourced from Virginia-specific RSS feeds and Google News RSS, filtered for AI/technology/workforce relevance, then assessed by Claude against the scenario framework. Each article is tagged with the region it most affects and the scenario it signals toward.

signals.title: Tech Briefs: Virginia Tech adds an artificial intelligence minor to its curriculum
signals.signal_reading: Virginia Tech launching an AI minor creates deep capability infrastructure in a non-metro region, potentially seeding distributed expertise through a major public university accessible to students across economic backgrounds.

signals.title: Norfolk native brings free AI workshops to Hampton Roads to close the technology gap - WTKR
signals.signal_reading: Free community AI workshops targeting the 'technology gap' represent grassroots capability-building outside elite institutions, signaling peer-to-peer knowledge distribution that could democratize foundational AI fluency in a historically maritime/military region.

signals.title: TAYLOR: AI data centers increase Virginia’s urban-rural divide - The Cavalier Daily
signals.signal_reading: Direct commentary on data centers increasing the urban-rural divide captures the structural risk that AI infrastructure concentrates economic benefits in NoVA while extracting resources (land, energy, tax breaks) from regions seeing neither workforce development nor capability gains.

signals.title: Children’s National and Virginia Tech deepen pediatric AI collaboration to accelerate innovation for children - Children's National
signals.signal_reading: Children's National-Virginia Tech partnership concentrates pediatric AI R&D capacity between two elite institutions, creating deep specialized expertise but signaling metro hub gravity rather than distributed healthcare AI capability across underserved rural Virginia communities.

signals.title: Tony Stark’s J.A.R.V.I.S., meet Amelia, Norfolk Naval Shipyard’s IT AI help assistant - MilitaryNews.com
signals.signal_reading: Norfolk Naval Shipyard deploying an AI help assistant represents platform-driven adoption that enables task completion without building deep AI literacy among workers—shallow but functional integration that could spread across federal facilities without creating local expertise depth.
